changeRequests.protocol: A UI role that needs a change to a shared entrypoint does not edit it. It opens a change request naming the file, the change (the exact markup or Forma-token rule) and the task it serves; integration applies it in its own pull request, in order, and the requesting role reviews that pull request. UI roles own their view modules (src/Causa.App/Views/*) and component-level presentation; the entrypoints only load them.
changeRequests.record: a Praxis work item owned by integration whose title starts with CR- and names the file, linked to the requesting task's work item
changeRequests.ruleSentence: It changes `web/index.html` and `web/causa.css` only through a change request to integration

startingState.residualRisk: The published rules say the repository starts empty and code starts at kickoff. They do not say whether material prepared before kickoff in executable form counts as planning or as code. Four kinds of material are at issue: the F# contract declarations, the deterministic generator, the layout assertions, and what conditor init writes at T0. conditor init writes the Echelon scaffold and imports 68 requirement documents (42 from this planning repository at commit 2eee2d5, 26 from Percepta). HACKATHON-BOUNDARIES lists, as an open question, whether a separate planning repository may be consumed directly by the blank implementation repository. The plan's boundary is that nothing is written to the competition repository before T0, and that everything written at T0 comes from approved, published sources. An organizer could read the materialized contract declarations, the Conditor scaffold, the requirements import, or the bootstrap itself as material prepared before kickoff. The plan does not claim otherwise. Whether organizer approval of the prepared material (ADRP-016-O2) is sought, and how it and R0.1-O1 are reported, is the owner's decision ODR-V411-02; the package as proposed does not seek it. If an organizer rules on the day, the team follows the ruling.
